The clustered heatmap is the default way to look at an expression matrix: rows and columns
reordered by similarity, dendrograms on the margins, and sample metadata alongside. In this
post we build one in R with [canvasXpress](https://canvasxpress.org) — clustering happens
inside the render, so you pass a plain matrix and get an interactive, reproducible figure.

## An expression matrix with sample metadata

Swap this simulated block for your own matrix (genes in rows, samples in columns) and a table
of per-sample annotations — the output of any normalization/DE pipeline works.

```{r}
#| message: false
library(canvasXpress)

set.seed(1)
ng    <- 40                       # genes (rows)
ns    <- 30                       # samples (columns)
genes <- paste0("Gene", seq_len(ng))
samps <- paste0("S", seq_len(ns))
cond  <- rep(c("Tumor", "Normal"), each = ns / 2)

# Two gene blocks, up in one condition each
m <- matrix(rnorm(ng * ns), ng, ns, dimnames = list(genes, samps))
m[ 1:20, cond == "Tumor"]  <- m[ 1:20, cond == "Tumor"]  + 2
m[21:40, cond == "Normal"] <- m[21:40, cond == "Normal"] + 2
```

canvasXpress takes the matrix as `data` and a **sample annotation** table (rows = samples)
that becomes an annotation track over the columns.

```{r}
smpAnnot <- data.frame(Condition = cond, row.names = samps, check.names = FALSE)
```

## The plot

`samplesClustered` and `variablesClustered` turn on hierarchical clustering (with
dendrograms) on columns and rows; `colorSpectrum` sets the diverging palette.

```{r}
canvasXpress(
  data     = as.data.frame(m),
  smpAnnot = smpAnnot,
  graphType = "Heatmap",
  samplesClustered  = TRUE,
  variablesClustered = TRUE,
  colorSpectrum = list("navy", "white", "firebrick3"),
  showSmpDendrogram = TRUE,
  showVarDendrogram = TRUE,
  title = "Clustered expression heatmap",
  width  = 650,
  height = 550
)
```

The rows and columns are reordered by similarity, the dendrograms show the clustering, and
the samples separate cleanly by condition. Hover a cell for its gene, sample and value; the
whole figure is one portable spec you can store, validate and re-render.

## Scaling up

The same call handles much larger matrices — hundreds of genes by dozens to hundreds of
samples — clustering and rendering the full matrix interactively in the browser, not a static
image. Point size and labels adapt automatically.
